programme: A lipid-handling / mitochondrial-oxidative metabolic switch built from AEBP1 (targeting the lipid-uptake and inflammatory genes APOE, CD36, FABP4, TNF) together with PPARGC1A/PGC-1α (targeting the mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative-metabolism genes TFAM, NRF1, CYCS, COX4I1, COX5B, SOD2, MFN2, plus lipid/glucose-handling genes LDLR, APOA5, ALDOB, SLC2A4). Both factors converge on the same class of lipid-uptake/oxidative genes even though they are not a physical complex.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, AEBP1 tracks with a lipid-laden, disease-associated microglial phenotype shift and with dysregulated astrocyte/cortex expression in late-onset AD (PMID 41516171, PMID 38568322, PMID 38345650), while PPARGC1A tracks with the oxidative-stress and impaired glucose-metabolism signature seen in AD brain (PMID 40642087) — together consistent with a glial bioenergetic/lipid-clearance failure accompanying neurodegeneration.
role_in_b: In thyroid cancer, AEBP1 directly promotes papillary thyroid cancer progression by activating BMP4 signaling (PMID 38237535). PPARGC1A appears in thyroid cancer gene-expression signatures in the retrieved record, but no paper here resolves what it is doing there functionally.
shared_axis: A cell under metabolic stress — a stressed/reactive glial cell in the AD brain, or a proliferating thyroid tumor cell — may repurpose the same lipid-uptake and mitochondrial-biogenesis machinery to meet altered energy and membrane-lipid demands, with AEBP1 and PGC-1α acting as two independent transcriptional entry points into that machinery rather than as a single documented pathway.
reasoning: AEBP1 has multiple functionally specific papers placing it independently in AD (microglial/astrocyte lipid-inflammatory phenotype) and in thyroid cancer (BMP4-driven progression), and both diseases carry an Open Targets association for it, so each disease's involvement of this factor is separately grounded rather than assumed. PPARGC1A strengthens the metabolic reading in AD but its thyroid-cancer role is only signature-level and unresolved in the record, and no source states the two diseases share this axis together — so the pairing itself is inference, not a retrieved fact, capping this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 41516171 (AEBP1 shifts microglial phenotype in AD); PMID 38568322 (AEBP1 dysregulated in late-onset AD cortex); PMID 38345650 (AEBP1 among neurotoxic astrocyte markers in AD); PMID 38237535 (AEBP1 promotes papillary thyroid cancer via BMP4 signaling); PMID 40642087 (PPARGC1A linked to oxidative stress/glucose metabolism in AD). No PMID here supports a PPARGC1A mechanism specifically in thyroid cancer.
how_to_falsify: Knock down AEBP1 in a reactive-microglia/astrocyte model and confirm whether CD36/FABP4/APOE induction depends on it; separately knock down AEBP1 in a papillary thyroid cancer line and confirm whether BMP4-pathway activity and invasion drop. If AEBP1's target program in the glial context does not overlap with lipid/oxidative genes (or PPARGC1A knockdown does not change mitochondrial/oxidative gene expression) in either tissue, or if AEBP1's thyroid mechanism turns out to be BMP4-specific with no lipid-handling component at all, the shared metabolic-axis account fails and AEBP1 is simply acting through two unrelated, tissue-specific programmes.
caveats: Brain and thyroid share no obvious anatomy or clinical pathway, and the 184 patient-group comparisons come from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance fraction mostly reflects robustness across clinical subgroupings within a small number of true replications, not many independent confirmations. A neuroendocrine/neural-crest story built on INSM1, SOX4, MYCN and LMX1A was considered (INSM1 marks medullary thyroid carcinoma and tracks with AD model gene expression; SOX4 drives thyroid tumorigenesis) but was set aside: SOX10, the master neural-crest regulator that would anchor that theme, was explicitly removed as tissue-generic, and MYCN/LMX1A have no credible disease-specific evidence in either dataset, per the reader's overall note. NFKBIB, MLX and DMAP1 have the highest recurrence (134-136/184) but no credible disease evidence for either condition and are not used here. FOXA2 and MYOCD were also excluded from the programme for lack of paired evidence.
